outOfScope: Changing BB-061 ContextRequirement, ContextResolution, resolutionId or Core pre-render resolution semantics.
Changing BB-062 SourceCatalog/provider/planner contracts except consuming their authoritative observations and derivation metadata.
Adding a mutable current-resolution head, lockfile-owned cache head or database solely for cache correctness.
Adding SQLite, Graphiti, Cognee, Redis or other persistence runtime dependencies in the foundation.
Automatic unbounded retry/progressive retrieval, durable model conversation memory or garbage collection as correctness logic.
Moving product/domain scheduling, acceptance, publication, claim recovery or external-effect authority into Oracle.
constraints: Durable reuse identity is separate from BB-061 semantic resolutionId; storage/backend details must not redefine semantic result identity.
Reuse begins from authoritative source observations supplied through the BB-062 source-authority boundary; provider/index self-observation cannot certify CURRENT.
A cache hit and a fresh materialization both require matching pre/post authoritative observations at the consumption boundary.
No reusable slot is published for UNSATISFIED required context; PARTIAL is reusable only when every unresolved optional need has a strongly fenced negative observation.
Manifest-protected application-artifact reads continue through the existing validating reader and receipt persistence cannot substitute for producer/revision/acceptance/content checks.
Concurrent same-key semantically divergent results fail closed instead of last-writer-wins.
Process-crash recovery is in scope; arbitrary machine/power-loss guarantees beyond the selected filesystem sync contract are not claimed.
Worker execution remains unauthorized until researchGaps are empty and a new exact Jev readiness judgment is SATISFIED.
invariants: Application/domain controllers own work semantics, acceptance, publication, recovery and product authority; Oracle only resolves context.
Every ContextResolution is bounded by explicit requirement/budget and preserves source provenance/currentness; missing or ambiguous required evidence fails closed.
Oracle is infrastructure-owned and provider/planner internals do not become model-visible scheduling authority or Core/Application implementation ownership.
architectureDecisions: D1 — Preserve BB-061 resolutionId unchanged. Add ContextResolutionReuseKey as sha256(canonical(requirementId + resolverConfigDigest + normalized sourceObservations + derivationInputs)).

D2 — Define SourceObservation v1 with evidenceId, source identity/mode/requested snapshot, observed state, exact observedSnapshotRef when present, validators, authorityRef/authorityRevision and optional provenanceDigest. REQUIRED CURRENT PRESENT requires at least one STRONG validator.

D3 — Define ResolverConfiguration v1 containing only semantics-affecting contract/planner/materialization/provider binding revisions. Timing, worker id, retry count and provider-call cost are excluded from reuse identity.
D4 — Define DerivationInput v1 for provider/operation/revision/providerSnapshotRef/configDigest. Derived/index/graph observations never replace authoritative source observations.

D5 — Define ContextResolutionReceipt v1 binding reuseKey, requirementId, resolutionId, materializationId, exact resolutionArtifactRef, resolverConfigDigest, sourceObservations, derivationInputs and itemLineage. receiptId hashes all semantic receipt fields except itself.

D6 — Every materialized item has one lineage record mapping itemDigest to authoritative sourceObservationIds plus provenance refs. Graph-derived items must close over authoritative source observations; graph/index identity alone is insufficient.

D7 — Persist canonical ContextResolution and receipt values as immutable content-addressed files. Publish by complete temp write + file sync/close + hard-link into digest-derived final name; existing exact content converges, digest/content mismatch fails closed.

D8 — Publish reusable cache entries into exact reuse/<reuseKey>.json no-overwrite slots containing reuseKey, resolutionId and receiptRef. Same reuseKey+same resolutionId converges; same reuseKey+different resolutionId is NONDETERMINISTIC_RESOLUTION_CONFLICT.

D9 — No mutable current cache head is used. Current lookup first observes authoritative sources, computes the exact reuseKey, then looks up that key. Source/currentness change therefore selects a different key without mutating old history.

D10 — Cache-hit and fresh paths both double-fence currentness: authoritative pre-observation before lookup/materialization and post-observation before reuse publication/consumption must have identical normalized digest. Drift produces STALE_DURING_RESOLUTION and no current consumption/publication.

D11 — COMPLETE is reusable when all fences/digests/lineage validate. PARTIAL is reusable only when all unresolved OPTIONAL evidence has strongly versioned negative observations. UNSATISFIED is never reusable.

D12 — Selective invalidation is logical, not destructive: evaluateReceiptCurrentness returns CURRENT|STALE plus changedEvidenceIds/reasons. Old immutable receipts remain historical evidence and are excluded by changed reuse keys.

D13 — Existing createManifestArtifactReader remains the authority for accepted-artifact payload validation. Durable SourceObservation/lineage adds exact manifest/provenance binding after that validation and cannot bypass it.

D14 — Crash after resolution/receipt object write but before reuse-slot publication leaves only an orphan immutable object. Retry may reuse exact bytes and publish; no partial object becomes canonical.

D15 — A stale writer whose source state changed cannot publish/consume current because the post-observation fence fails. Even an old-key historical slot can never satisfy a reader that observes a newer key.

D16 — Persistence backend selected for foundation is the filesystem immutable-object + no-overwrite exact-key slot design, modeled on the current manifest store. Mutable lockfile CAS is rejected for cache currentness because crash can strand the lock and a mutable head is unnecessary.

D17 — Restic/Git/Bazel evidence supports immutable content-addressed artifacts and key/reference separation. node:sqlite is evaluated but not selected; current Node source marks it release-candidate and the no-head design does not need transactional mutable state.
D18 — No automatic retry loop is introduced. Currentness drift is explicit failure; a later bounded resolution call/step may retry under normal BB-061 budget/progression semantics.
implementationSlices: S1 [DURABLE_CONTRACTS,INV-2] — After BB-061/062 dependency outputs exist, add strict SourceObservation, ResolverConfiguration, DerivationInput and ContextResolutionReceipt v1 contracts plus canonical observationDigest, resolverConfigDigest, reuseKey and receiptId helpers. Extend dependency-created packages/oracle/src/index.js rather than creating parallel contract surfaces.

S2 [LINEAGE,CURRENTNESS,INV-2] — Validate one itemLineage record per ContextResolution item; every lineage sourceObservationId must exist; graph/derived items must reach at least one authoritative observation. Implement evaluateReceiptCurrentness(receipt,currentObservations) returning CURRENT|STALE with exact changedEvidenceIds/reasons. CURRENT PRESENT requires exact snapshot + strong validator; stable ABSENT requires authorityRevision.

S3 [IMMUTABLE_STORE] — Add resolution-store.js with content-addressed immutable resolution/receipt objects and exact reuse-key slots. Final objects/slots appear only after complete temp write + sync/close + hard-link no-overwrite. Read validates filename/ref digest and strict artifact contract. Same reuseKey+same resolutionId converges; semantic divergence under one key fails NONDETERMINISTIC_RESOLUTION_CONFLICT.

S4 [DURABLE_REUSE,RECOVERY] — Add a durability coordinator that asks the delivered BB-062 source-authority seam for normalized pre-observations, computes reuseKey, validates any exact-key cached receipt/materialization, obtains post-observations before consumption, and otherwise materializes fresh through the delivered resolver then repeats the post-fence before publishing. Observation drift returns STALE_DURING_RESOLUTION; no automatic retry loop is hidden inside the coordinator.

S5 [REUSE_POLICY] — Publish reusable slots only for COMPLETE, or PARTIAL where every unresolved OPTIONAL need has a strongly fenced negative observation. Never publish UNSATISFIED, currentness-unverifiable, ambiguous-required or partial-provider-failure REQUIRED results. Cache reuse remains optional and cannot change acceptance/domain state.

S6 [MANIFEST_COMPAT,INV-1] — Add integration fixtures that continue to read accepted application artifacts through createManifestArtifactReader/manifest-protected Backend->QA semantics, then bind exact manifest ref/digest, producer revision, acceptance decision, stored revision/content digest into SourceObservation/lineage. Matching bytes with wrong provenance must still fail before reusable receipt publication.

S7 [FAILURE_INJECTION,INV-3] — Add deterministic crash/concurrency tests: 20 same-key equivalent publishers converge to one slot; same-key different resolutionId conflicts; crash after resolution object and after receipt object but before slot leaves harmless orphan and retry converges; source changes pre/post block publication; old-key stale writer cannot satisfy new-key lookup; corrupted object/slot/digest fails closed; simulated leftover lock demonstrates the rejected lockfile-head failure mode.

S8 [CURRENTNESS_PROBE] — Add bb063-currentness-probe.mjs with repository CURRENT A->A and A->B cases, exact accepted-artifact manifest replay, semantic-index snapshot equal/mismatch, graph-derived lineage with authoritative leaves, stable/unstable optional absence, partial provider failure and concurrent refresh. Emit exact reuse keys/currentness reasons and all attempts.

S9 [LIVING_TRUTH] — Update Oracle Living Docs with durable receipt/reuse semantics and limitations: no mutable current resolution head, no SQLite/graph DB dependency, no failure-cache authority, no garbage-collection correctness and no power-loss guarantee beyond the implemented fs sync contract.

negativeVerificationCases: Durable reuse logic changes BB-061 resolutionId by adding storage/backend/config details.
A cache reader trusts reuse slot or provider/index self-report without authoritative pre/post source observations.
Required CURRENT evidence has only weak/timestamp validation or provider snapshot differs from authoritative source and is still reusable.
Source changes between pre-observation and prompt consumption but cached/fresh resolution is returned as current.
UNSATISFIED or required partial-provider failure publishes a reusable slot.
PARTIAL with optional unresolved evidence lacking strongly versioned negative observation publishes a reusable slot.
Same reuseKey accepts two different semantic resolutionIds by last-writer-wins.
Crash leaves a partial final object/slot that later reads as canonical.
Corrupted resolution/receipt bytes or ref/digest mismatch are accepted.
Graph-derived item has no authoritative source-observation lineage.
Manifest-compatible bytes with wrong producer/revision/acceptance/stored revision become reusable.
Durability layer claims work, accepts/publishes product state, recovers domain claims or mutates external effects.
Worker introduces a mutable lockfile cache head, SQLite/Graphiti/Cognee dependency or hidden automatic retry loop.
Living Docs claim BB-064 foundation acceptance, garbage collection or power-loss durability beyond implemented sync semantics.

durabilityContract.reuseIdentity: reuseKey = sha256(canonical(requirementId + resolverConfigDigest + sourceObservations + derivationInputs)); BB-061 resolutionId remains unchanged.
durabilityContract.receipt: ContextResolutionReceipt binds reuseKey, requirementId, resolutionId, materializationId, resolutionArtifactRef, resolverConfigDigest, sourceObservations, derivationInputs and per-item lineage.
durabilityContract.store: Immutable content-addressed resolution/receipt objects plus exact no-overwrite reuse-key slot; no mutable current-resolution head.
durabilityContract.currentnessFence: Authoritative pre/post observation digests must match before cache-hit or fresh result can be consumed/published as current.
durabilityContract.reusePolicy: COMPLETE reusable; PARTIAL only with strongly fenced optional negative observations; UNSATISFIED never reusable.
durabilityContract.invalidation: Logical selective currentness evaluation returns changedEvidenceIds/reasons; historical immutable receipts are not destructively rewritten.

researchEvidence.finding: Existing manifest persistence uses digest-bound immutable content plus temp-write/hard-link no-overwrite publication and explicit concurrent semantic conflict handling.
Existing JSON CAS head uses an exclusive lock file around mutation; a process crash can strand that lock unless an additional recovery protocol exists.
Existing product lineage keeps immutable journal artifacts authoritative and uses exact head observations/currentness checks; demonstrates immutable-history/currentness separation.

Durable Backend->QA recovery persists exact accepted handoff/manifest refs and fences interrupted execution through application claim generation; Oracle receipt reuse must not weaken that continuation.
Restic design uses SHA-256 storage IDs, write-once immutable repository files and atomic writes for concurrent access.
Bazel remote cache separates Action Cache lookup entries from Content Addressable Storage blobs; useful analogy for reuse key versus immutable result object.
Git repository layout separates content-addressed objects from refs/current tips; BB-063 keeps the object lesson but avoids a mutable cache-current ref.
node:sqlite is available but current source marks the module Stability 1.2 / release candidate; no mutable DB is required by the selected exact-key reuse design.
